papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics in immune-mediated necrotising myopathy uncovers a specific necrotic signature related to immune-driven fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotising myopathies (IMNM) are characterised by muscle fibre necrosis, complement deposits around non-necrotic fibres, and macrophage infiltrates. Patients experience muscle damage with fibro-fatty replacement, leading to poor strength recovery, but the pathogenesis remains unclear. To investigate IMNM pathogenesis, we applied spatial transcriptomics on myositis muscle biopsies and integrated the results with published single-nucleus transcriptomic data. This combined approach enabled analysis of gene expression with spatial localisation in the muscle. Inflammatory, fibrotic
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics on muscle biopsies from patients with immune-mediated necrotising myopathy, integrated with published single-nucleus RNA-seq data, to map gene expression to specific tissue regions. The authors identified a distinct necrosis-associated transcriptional signature linked to immune-driven fibrosis, offering new insight into why patients suffer fibro-fatty replacement and poor strength recovery.

papers.title: YAP/AP-1 Activation in Sebocytes Promotes CCL5-Dependent Perifollicular Macrophage Recruitment in Rosacea.
papers.abstract: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder in which macrophages have been increasingly implicated, yet the spatial basis and local cues of their recruitment remain poorly defined. Given the prominent perifollicular inflammatory changes in rosacea, we investigated whether sebocytes contribute to macrophage recruitment and the underlying mechanisms. Multiplex immunofluorescence combined with distance-stratified quantification demonstrated a preferential perifollicular distribution of macrophages around pilosebaceous units (PSUs) in human rosacea lesions. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencin
papers.summary: This study shows that in rosacea, macrophages cluster preferentially around hair follicles and sebaceous glands. Sebocytes in these structures activate YAP/AP-1 signaling, which drives production of the chemokine CCL5 and recruits macrophages to the perifollicular niche. The work defines a spatial and molecular axis linking sebocyte signaling to immune cell recruitment in rosacea.

papers.title: An interpretable deep learning framework for revealing fine-grained spatial domains.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables gene expression profiling with preserved spatial context, yet accurate spatial domain delineation remains challenging. We present RIF, a robust and interpretable deep learning framework for fine-grained spatial domain identification. RIF leverages graph neural networks semi-supervised with pseudo-labels to preserve tissue structural integrity. It incorporates a dual-preprocessing ensemble strategy to improve model robustness and generalization. It further enables spatially variable gene detection through network interpretability. Across multiple sequencing platf
papers.summary: RIF is a deep learning framework that identifies fine-grained spatial domains in spatial transcriptomics data by combining graph neural networks with semi-supervised pseudo-labeling and a dual-preprocessing ensemble strategy. It also detects spatially variable genes through network interpretability, and the authors demonstrate its performance across multiple sequencing platforms.

papers.title: STRAND: a comprehensive subcellular-resolved spatial transcriptome RNA architecture and navigation database.
papers.abstract: Subcellular RNA localization serves as a critical regulatory layer governing cellular polarization, local translation, and functional compartmentalization. Recent advances in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented opportunities to resolve these intracellular architectures at single-molecule resolution. However, relevant datasets are dispersed across studies and repositories, vary substantially in processing procedures and standards, severely limiting their cross-study reuse. To bridge this gap, we present STRAND (Subcellular-Resolved Spatial Transcriptome RNA Archi
papers.summary: STRAND is a new database that collects and standardizes subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics datasets, addressing the fragmentation of RNA localization data across studies. It provides a unified resource for exploring intracellular RNA architecture and navigation, enabling cross-study reuse of single-molecule localization data.

papers.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n
papers.summary: This review categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from static scRNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. It highlights that these methods rely on different, sometimes contrasting assumptions, and provides a unified mathematical framework for comparing them. The work serves as a guide for choosing appropriate potency inference tools and understanding their limitations.

papers.title: Deciphering conserved and divergent tissue architectures via soDGVAE-mediated spatial transcriptomics integration.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics has revolutionized our understanding of molecular heterogeneity within its native tissue context. However, the integrative analysis of datasets spanning replicate samples, disparate platforms, different developmental stages, and cross-species remains a challenging computational task.
papers.summary: The authors present soDGVAE, a deep generative model for integrating spatial transcriptomics datasets across replicates, platforms, developmental stages, and species. The method aims to separate conserved tissue architectures from species- or condition-specific divergence, enabling comparative spatial analysis that was previously difficult due to batch and platform effects.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral arter
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing across three post-stroke timepoints with spatial transcriptomics at day 7 to map how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell treatment relates to neuroimmune and neuronal signaling after ischemic stroke in mice. The authors generate a large single-cell atlas (55,520 cells) revealing cell-type-specific and spatially heterogeneous responses, providing a resource for understanding MSC-associated modulation of secondary injury and repair.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Multi-Omics Reveals Primate-Specific Mechanisms of Liver Regeneration Following Partial Hepatectomy.
papers.abstract: The liver is a vital metabolic organ with an extraordinary capacity for regeneration, making it a key focus for understanding tissue repair and developing therapeutic strategies for liver diseases. However, ethical limitations restrict liver regeneration research largely to rodents, leaving critical gaps in our understanding of primate-specific mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses spatiotemporal multi-omics profiling to characterize liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in a primate model, addressing a gap left by rodent-only research. The authors identify primate-specific molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying tissue repair, which may inform therapeutic strategies for human liver disease.

papers.title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. The current release con
papers.summary: CellMarker 3.0 is an updated database that combines manually curated, experimentally validated cell marker genes with computationally predicted markers for many cell types in human and mouse tissues. It adds substantial new content over the prior version and introduces interactive web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data. The resource aims to help researchers identify and annotate cell types in single-cell and spatial studies.

papers.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
papers.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat
papers.summary: The authors developed droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing methods, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT, by combining a commercial microfluidic device with nanopore sequencing to profile chromatin accessibility and histone modifications in individual cells at high throughput. This addresses the scalability limitations of prior long-read single-cell epigenomic approaches, enabling multidimensional regulatory element profiling per cell.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics identifies tumor-intrinsic and stromal programs associated with immune exclusion in NSCLC.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has reshaped the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable benefit remains limited to a subset of patients. One major pattern of resistance is immune exclusion, in which CD8+ T cells accumulate in stromal regions but fail to penetrate tumor nests. Here, using discovery and non-overlapping internal validation cohorts of ICB-treated NSCLC patients, we show that spatial CD8+ T-cell exclusion is associated with lower objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival. To characterize the molecular programs linked to this phen
papers.summary: Using spatial transcriptomics on ICB-treated NSCLC cohorts, the authors show that CD8+ T-cell exclusion from tumor nests predicts poor response and shorter progression-free survival. They identify distinct tumor-intrinsic and stromal gene programs associated with this immune-excluded phenotype, offering candidate mechanisms of ICB resistance.

papers.title: CCCView: A Knowledge Platform for Integrated Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomic Cell-Cell Communication.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of cell-cell communication (CCC) while preserving spatial context, yet large-scale resources that organize spatial CCC results across studies and make them readily searchable, visualizable, and comparable remain limited. Here, we present CCCView, a knowledge platform integrating 699 spatial transcriptomics samples and 7,473,444 inferred CCC interactions across 24 tissues, 182 annotated cell types, and 27 biological conditions in human and mouse. CCCView uses a unified cell-type annotation workflow and organizes results from three complementary CCC-
papers.summary: CCCView is a new knowledge platform that aggregates cell-cell communication (CCC) inferences from 699 spatial transcriptomics samples, yielding over 7.4 million interactions across 24 tissues, 182 cell types, and 27 biological conditions in human and mouse. It standardizes cell-type annotation and organizes results from three complementary CCC methods, making spatial communication data searchable, visualizable, and comparable across studies. This addresses the lack of large-scale, integrated resources for spatial CCC analysis.

papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small
papers.summary: This protocol describes an optimized workflow for preparing small, structurally complex plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics, covering cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, precise section placement on capture slides, and downstream data analysis. It addresses the practical bottlenecks of rapid preservation, orientation, and positioning that have limited spatial transcriptomics in plant developmental studies.

papers.title: A Cross-Condition Single-Cell Atlas Defines Skeletal Muscle Adaptation and Its Predictive Limits.
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle adapts to diverse stresses through coordinated changes across myofibres and cellular niches, yet these responses are usually studied separately. We assembled a cross-species discovery atlas of 501,940 cells and nuclei from six public resources, comprising 2863 condition-time-state combinations defined at the declared analysis unit level, and evaluated it with two independent validation datasets. Injury produced the largest observed compositional displacement, followed by mechanical overload, whereas acute human endurance exercise and denervation showed smaller occupancy shifts
papers.summary: This study assembled a large cross-species single-cell atlas of skeletal muscle (501,940 cells and nuclei from six public resources) covering many condition-time-state combinations, and validated it against two independent datasets. Injury caused the largest compositional shifts in cell populations, followed by mechanical overload, while acute endurance exercise and denervation produced smaller changes. The atlas defines muscle adaptation patterns and also probes the limits of predicting responses across conditions.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data into distinct malignant cell states, addressing intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity without requiring single-cell reference data. By resolving cell-state composition from bulk transcriptomes, it offers a scalable alternative to scRNA-seq for studying heterogeneity across large cancer cohorts. This could enable broader analyses of how cell-state diversity affects treatment response.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omic Analysis of Paired Primary and Peritoneal Metastatic Tumors Reveals GPAA1 as a Therapeutic Target in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis confers a dismal prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC-PM), with median survival rarely exceeding 20 months. Here we employed multi-omic profiling to identify actionable drivers of CRC-PM. We performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) and label-free quantitative proteomics on 13 and 7 matched primary-peritoneal metastasis pairs, respectively. Public single-cell (GSE183916 and GSE132465) and spatial transcriptomic datasets (GSE225857) were integrated to dissect cellular heterogeneity. TCGA cohorts were used for survival analysis, and functional validation was performed in DLD1 c
papers.summary: This study combined whole-exome sequencing and proteomics on matched primary and peritoneal metastatic colorectal cancer samples, supplemented with public single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data, to identify drivers of peritoneal metastasis. The integrated analysis pinpointed GPAA1 as a candidate therapeutic target, supported by TCGA survival associations and functional validation in colorectal cancer cell lines. The work highlights how multi-omic profiling of matched tumor pairs can reveal actionable metastasis-specific vulnerabilities.

papers.title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. Methods: We propose the CQRM, an adaptive multi-quantile testing framework for ncRNA count data that incorporates jittering to accommodate discrete cou
papers.summary: The authors propose CQRM, a composite quantile regression framework for differential expression analysis of non-coding RNA count data. It uses adaptive multi-quantile testing with jittering to handle the discrete, low-expression, and highly variable nature of ncRNA counts, addressing limitations of standard DE methods for these data.

papers.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
papers.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from c
papers.summary: This review synthesizes knowledge about tenocytes (tendon cells) and their surrounding matrix as one integrated system spanning eight orders of magnitude in scale. It connects five levels—collagen chemistry, molecular mechanics, fibril/fascicle structure, tissue loading, and cellular mechanotransduction to transcription—arguing that these have been studied in disconnected literatures. The authors propose a multiscale causal framework linking chemistry, mechanics, cell biology, and mathematical modeling.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, a parasite causing visceral leishmaniasis. They then profiled the transcriptome of these cells, providing the first gene expression signature for MGCs in this infection context. This work offers insight into how these poorly understood cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to build a compact risk score predicting pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma, centered on a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated program. The work links a specific gene signature to reduced immune activity and identifies single-cell programs associated with metastatic risk.

papers.title: Beyond Histocompatibility: Donor Tissue Immune States and Their Role in Heart Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Heart transplantation transfers not only donor alloantigens and functional myocardium but also a pre-existing tissue environment shaped by resident immune, vascular, stromal, and parenchymal populations. This review examines the hypothesis that the biological state of donor tissue influences subsequent recipient immunity and contributes to heterogeneity in allograft outcomes. Donor-resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and tissue-resident lymphocytes constitute an immunologically active myocardial niche that encounters ischemia-reperfusion injury and recip
papers.summary: This review argues that donor hearts bring more than just alloantigens to transplant recipients—they carry a pre-existing immune environment of resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and tissue-resident lymphocytes. The authors propose that this donor tissue immune state, together with ischemia-reperfusion injury, shapes how the recipient's immune system responds and may explain why transplant outcomes vary so much between patients.

papers.title: Pan-Cancer Analysis Identifies LUC7L2 as a Prognostic Biomarker and Potential Functional Regulator of Prostate Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer imposes a substantial global public health burden, and its initiation and progression involve complex dysregulation of gene expression regulatory networks. Methods: This study systematically evaluated the expression characteristics and prognostic value of LUC7L2 across pan-cancer types, with a particular focus on functional validation in prostate cancer. Using transcriptomic and proteomic data from multiple databases, immunohistochemical staining from the Human Protein Atlas, and single-cell transcriptomic datasets GSE137829 and GSE176031, we analyzed the expressi
papers.summary: This study analyzes LUC7L2 expression across multiple cancer types using transcriptomic, proteomic, and single-cell data, finding it has prognostic value and is particularly relevant in prostate cancer. Functional validation suggests LUC7L2 may regulate prostate cancer progression, positioning it as a potential biomarker.

papers.title: Spathology: The Birth of Spatial Pathology as a Discipline.
papers.abstract: Pathology has always been a spatial science: for more than 150 years, diagnosis has rested on reading the architecture of cells and tissues. Three technological streams are now converging on this founding principle. Spatially resolved omics can measure thousands of transcripts and over a hundred proteins in intact, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue; multiplexed imaging quantifies tissue microenvironments cell by cell; and computational pathology has progressed from slide digitization to foundation models that can predict molecular features from morphology. The clinical evidence fo
papers.summary: This perspective argues that spatial pathology is emerging as a distinct discipline from the convergence of spatially resolved omics, multiplexed imaging, and computational pathology foundation models. It traces how these technologies extend pathology's long-standing spatial tradition to molecular and computational scales, and reviews emerging clinical evidence for their use.

papers.title: scStable: assessing scRNA-seq analysis stability under bulk-derived between-sample variation.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies often profile only one or a few biological samples, limiting assessment of discovery stability under between-sample variation. We present scStable, a framework for assessing scRNA-seq analysis stability by generating synthetic samples that preserve cell-level heterogeneity from a single-sample reference while injecting bulk-derived between-sample variation. In gastric cancer data comprising 21 matched scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq profiles, scStable better recapitulates observed between-sample variation than ZINB-WaVE, subsampling, and Gaussian noise
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: scStable is a new computational framework that tests how stable scRNA-seq analysis results are when between-sample biological variation is present, even if only one sample was sequenced. It creates synthetic samples by keeping the original cell-level heterogeneity while adding variation learned from matched bulk RNA-seq data. In gastric cancer data with 21 matched single-cell and bulk profiles, scStable reproduced real between-sample variation better than existing methods like ZINB-WaVE, subsampling, and Gaussian noise.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The paper introduces CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq data into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then uses this to infer drug sensitivity from bulk transcriptomes. This enables mapping of single-cell signals to bulk samples, allowing drug response to be resolved at cell-type resolution rather than as an aggregate. The approach addresses the problem of bulk measurements obscuring cell-specific signals in heterogeneous tissues.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to characterize cell adhesion-related gene expression patterns in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identify cell-type-specific and bulk-level gene signatures linked to inflammatory infiltration and blood-brain barrier disruption, nominating candidate therapeutic targets. The work is primarily descriptive and computational, relying on existing datasets without experimental validation.

papers.title: Protocol for reference-free single-cell-resolution deconvolution of spot-based spatial transcriptomics with CoexpressDeconvolve.
papers.abstract: Spot-based spatial transcriptomics captures whole-transcriptome signal per spot but mixes multiple cells. Here, we present a protocol for using CoexpressDeconvolve, a reference-free approach that reconstructs single-cell-resolution, whole-transcriptome profiles directly from spot-based spatial transcriptomics data. We describe steps for housekeeping-gene cell-density calibration, joint overdispersed-gene selection, a gene co-expression manifold, and automated topic-number selection. We then detail procedures for latent Dirichlet allocation, hierarchical Bayesian sampling, and exporting to a 10
papers.summary: This protocol describes CoexpressDeconvolve, a reference-free computational method that reconstructs single-cell-resolution, whole-transcriptome profiles from spot-based spatial transcriptomics data without needing external reference datasets. The workflow covers housekeeping-gene-based cell-density calibration, joint selection of overdispersed genes, construction of a gene co-expression manifold, automated topic-number selection, and latent Dirichlet allocation with hierarchical Bayesian sampling. It provides step-by-step guidance for users to deconvolve mixed-cell spots into single-cell profiles.

papers.title: Alveolar Type II Cell-derived MMP1high basal cells promote destructive microcysts in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Alveolar microcysts, a hallmark of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF), are basal cell (BC)-lined structures that develop near terminal airways and correlate with poor clinical outcomes. Using primary-cell organoids and spatial transcriptomics, we identified striking epithelial similarities between respiratory bronchioles (RBs) and IPF alveolar microcysts, both containing AT0 (ABCA3+/SCGB3A2+), SCGB3A2+, and basaloid/BC populations, although basaloid/BCs were markedly expanded in IPF microcysts. A CEACAM6+ subset of normal RB epithelial cells, termed respiratory airway secretory cells (RASCs),
papers.summary: Using primary-cell organoids and spatial transcriptomics, this study shows that alveolar microcysts in IPF closely resemble respiratory bronchioles, sharing AT0, SCGB3A2+, and basaloid/basal cell populations, with basaloid/basal cells markedly expanded in IPF microcysts. The authors identify an ATII-derived MMP1-high basal cell population that promotes destructive microcyst formation, implicating these cells in IPF pathogenesis.

papers.title: Stromal APOL4 defines a cancer-associated fibroblast state that organizes a chemosensitive niche in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Despite initial high response rates to platinum-based chemotherapy in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, most patients eventually develop resistance, and the contribution of the tumor microenvironment to treatment outcomes has remained underexplored relative to tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms. Combining patient-derived ex vivo carboplatin screening with bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, functional perturbation in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, we identified stromal apolipoprotein L4 (APOL4) as a biomarker of platinum sensitivity. The ex
papers.summary: This study identifies APOL4 expression in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) as a marker of platinum sensitivity in high-grade serous ovarian cancer. By combining ex vivo drug screening with bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, functional CAF perturbation, and spatial transcriptomics, the authors show that APOL4-positive CAFs organize a tumor microenvironment niche that promotes chemosensitivity. This highlights stromal, not just tumor-intrinsic, determinants of chemotherapy response.

papers.title: Cellular and spatial continuum of TAM functional states governs immune exclusion and dictates immune checkpoint resistance in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has transformed melanoma treatment, yet many patients either fail to respond or develop resistance after an initial response. The cellular and spatial determinants within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that underlie these divergent ICI therapy outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we aimed to characterize the immune composition and spatial organization of the TME associated with ICI response and resistance.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the immune composition and spatial organization of the melanoma tumor microenvironment to understand why some patients respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors while others develop resistance. The authors identify a continuum of tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) functional states whose spatial distribution governs immune exclusion and dictates ICI resistance. The work links specific cellular states and their spatial arrangement to clinical outcomes, offering potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: SpatioCAD: Context-aware graph diffusion model for pinpointing spatially variable genes in heterogeneous tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables comprehensive characterization of tissue architecture, and the identification of spatially variable genes (SVGs) is a critical step for defining region-specific molecular markers and uncovering spatially regulated mechanisms across diverse biological contexts. However, most existing methods for SVG detection overlook cell density variations, a major confounding factor in complex tissues such as tumors, where heterogeneous cellularity frequently introduces false-positive calls. Here we present SpatioCAD, a computational framework that explicitly decouples genuine
papers.summary: SpatioCAD is a new computational framework for identifying spatially variable genes (SVGs) in spatial transcriptomics data. It uses a context-aware graph diffusion model that explicitly accounts for cell density variations, a major confounder in heterogeneous tissues like tumors that can cause false-positive SVG calls. This approach aims to more accurately pinpoint genes with genuine spatial patterns.

papers.title: IsoPrism predicts isoform usage from short-read transcriptomes through structure-guided competitive allocation.
papers.abstract: Short-read (SR) single-cell and spatial transcriptomics characterize gene expression but provide limited resolution of within-gene isoform usage. Here we present IsoPrism, a structure-guided competitive allocation framework that predicts isoform proportions from gene-level expression. IsoPrism combines individual expression and local expression context with transcript structural annotations, using shared iterative updates to preserve non-negative, gene-normalized proportions. Joint supervision from individual long-read (LR) counts and group-level isoform usage enables prediction in samples wit
papers.summary: IsoPrism is a computational framework that predicts isoform usage proportions from gene-level short-read single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data. It combines individual expression levels, local expression context, and transcript structural annotations through iterative updates, trained with joint supervision from long-read counts and group-level isoform usage. This enables isoform resolution in samples lacking long-read data.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods so that method weighting varies by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also introduce a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, this score-level meta-classifier aims to resolve disagreements between methods more effectively than picking one method or simple averaging.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with machine learning to build a prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature (PIS) for non-small cell lung cancer based on epithelial cell-derived genes. The signature stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS patients showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. The authors validate ADAM12 as a highly expressed functional regulator through cell line assays and mouse experiments.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data into three groups: cell-type or single-cell resolution network inference, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability, and regulatory modulation. It highlights how spatial context enables more biologically grounded communication inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone and maps methods to the distinct biological questions they address.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors introduce a Contextual Activity Score (CAS) that infers ADAR-associated RNA editing activity from gene expression data rather than raw sequencing reads, overcoming the limitations of the standard Alu Editing Index for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. This enables estimation of ADAR activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial platforms where read-level editing quantification is impractical.

papers.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies NUDT21, a key regulator of alternative polyadenylation (APA), as a central node in an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that sustains neuroblastoma proliferation and survival. The work links APA-mediated post-transcriptional control to broader transcriptional programs in this pediatric cancer, suggesting that disrupting this circuit could be a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Identification of ageing-related genes in prostate cancer with type 2 Diabetes using machine learning: a multi-omics study focusing on SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) demonstrates complex associations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and ageing, though their interconnected molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify and validate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of these pathways to enable early detection and risk stratification in high-risk populations. Bioinformatic analysis was performed on PCa and T2DM transcriptomic data downloaded from the GEO database, followed by differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. Eight machi
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic datasets from prostate cancer and type 2 diabetes to identify shared ageing-related genes, using differential expression, WGCNA, and multiple machine-learning classifiers. The authors nominate SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4 as candidate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of ageing, T2DM, and prostate cancer, with subsequent validation analyses. The work is exploratory and biomarker-discovery oriented, relying on public GEO data.

papers.title: Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.
papers.abstract: Predicting single-gene knockout effects from wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging when perturbation experiments are costly and existing approaches require knockout-specific model training. Here we introduce Topology-Adjusted Knockout (TAKO), a computationally efficient WT-only framework for single-gene KO impact ranking on single-cell gene regulatory networks. The method applies a strict cut-in-and-out intervention on network transition dynamics and quantifies impact by contrasting stationary propagation profiles before and after perturbation under the same restart distributi
papers.summary: TAKO is a computational framework that predicts the impact of single-gene knockouts using only wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data, without requiring knockout-specific training. It works by applying a strict cut-in-and-out intervention on gene regulatory network transition dynamics and measuring how stationary propagation profiles change before and after perturbation. This enables interpretable in silico ranking of knockout effects at low computational cost.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identifies monocyte/macrophage senescence-associated candidate genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and vascular remodeling. Cellular senescence modulates immune responses, but its role in PAH, particularly in monocytes/macrophages, remains unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify senescence-associated candidate genes associated with monocytes/macrophages in PAH.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic datasets to identify senescence-associated genes specifically in monocytes/macrophages in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The authors propose candidate genes linking immune cell senescence to PAH vascular remodeling, though the findings are computational and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Compartment-resolved epithelial and myeloid programs are shared by pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) develops within a complex tumor microenvironment characterized by malignant epithelial states, myeloid inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. Related thrombo-inflammatory transcriptional features have also been observed in ischemic stroke, but whether these diseases share reproducible molecular programs, and how such programs are organized across cellular compartments in PDAC, remains incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: The authors compare transcriptional programs in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and ischemic stroke, finding shared epithelial and myeloid signatures organized by cellular compartment. This suggests common thrombo-inflammatory and epithelial-state programs across these otherwise distinct diseases.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal transcriptomic signatures of resident cardiac macrophages and macrophage-associated spatial states during acute myocardial infarction.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) followed by reperfusion result in a phasic response by cardiac macrophages. During the first 7 days after AMI, macrophage populations exhibit dynamic phenotypic changes. Ultimately, inflammatory damage results in ventricular remodeling and fibrosis. Macrophages are critical to cardiac function and long-term prognoses.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map how resident cardiac macrophages change over space and time in the first week after acute myocardial infarction and reperfusion. It identifies distinct macrophage-associated spatial states that accompany the transition from inflammation to ventricular remodeling and fibrosis. The work links macrophage phenotype to tissue location, offering a spatially resolved view of the post-infarct immune response.

papers.title: Multiomics Dissection of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer (EOCRC) Reveals an Immunosuppressive Microenvironment and Identifies FAT3 Mutation as a Biomarker of Hot-Like Immune Features.
papers.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) exhibits distinct clinical and biological features compared with late-onset CRC (LOCRC), yet its genomic architecture and immune microenvironmental determinants remain incompletely characterized. Here, we integrated multiomics discovery analyses of 69 EOCRC and 461 LOCRC patients from the TCGA cohort, complemented by independent validation, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and systems-level network analysis. We identified 10 genes significantly enriched for mutations in EOCRC, including ANXA7, ZNF267, and POLQ, which displayed distinct
papers.summary: This study integrates multiomics data from TCGA and independent cohorts to characterize early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), identifying 10 genes with significantly enriched mutations (including ANXA7, ZNF267, and POLQ) compared to late-onset CRC. The authors further show that EOCRC is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and that FAT3 mutations mark tumors with 'hot-like' immune features, suggesting FAT3 as a potential biomarker.

papers.title: Spatial multiomics identifies rheumatoid arthritis synovial niches and de-novo laminar histological patterns of fibroblasts subtypes.
papers.abstract: Spatial omic technologies provide insight into molecular architecture and spatial cellular organization within tissue. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), single-cell RNA sequencing and low-resolution spatial transcriptomics have advanced the understanding of synovial biology. However, single-cell spatial resolution using multiple spatial platforms to comprehensively map the immune and stromal cell organization as well as topographical cellular interactions in the RA synovium remain limited.
papers.summary: This study applies multiple spatial omics platforms at single-cell resolution to map the cellular organization of rheumatoid arthritis synovium, identifying distinct synovial niches and previously unrecognized laminar histological patterns formed by fibroblast subtypes. The work integrates immune and stromal cell spatial interactions to provide a more comprehensive topographical atlas of RA joint tissue than prior single-cell RNA-seq or low-resolution spatial transcriptomics approaches.

papers.title: Ferumoxytol potentiates ferroptotic radiosensitization through NCOA4-associated iron mobilization in brain-metastatic lung cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis remains a major cause of mortality in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer, whereas effective radiosensitization strategies are constrained by heterogeneous tumor responses and the tolerance of normal brain tissue. Ferumoxytol, a clinically used iron oxide nanoparticle formulation, has emerging translational potential as an iron-modulating agent. However, whether Ferumoxytol enhances radiosensitivity in brain-metastatic lung cancer cells and the mechanisms underlying this effect remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether ferumoxytol, an FDA-approved iron oxide nanoparticle, can sensitize brain-metastatic lung cancer cells to radiation. The authors propose that ferumoxytol promotes ferroptosis (iron-dependent cell death) by mobilizing iron through NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy, thereby enhancing radiosensitivity. The work suggests a potential repurposing strategy for improving radiotherapy in brain metastases.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis reveals the role of PGRN in modulating fibroblast heterogeneity and enhancing wound healing.
papers.abstract: The wound microenvironment plays a crucial role in the skin wound healing process. Fibroblasts, one of the critical cell types within this microenvironment, exhibit significant heterogeneity that influences healing outcomes. Previous studies have demonstrated that progranulin (PGRN) may reduce fibrogenesis during wound healing. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Thus, this study aims to investigate the specific effects of PGRN on fibroblast heterogeneity of skin wound healing in mice.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA-seq to examine how progranulin (PGRN) affects fibroblast heterogeneity during skin wound healing in mice. The authors find that PGRN modulates distinct fibroblast subpopulations, which may explain its previously observed anti-fibrotic effects and its ability to improve healing outcomes.

papers.title: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation.
papers.abstract: Glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) represent a recently recognized connection between RNA biology and cell-surface glycobiology. However, whether glycoRNA-related processes are relevant to human tumors remains unclear, partly because direct glycoRNA measurements are not yet available across large cancer cohorts. We therefore used transcriptomic data to identify tumor settings in which glycoRNA-related programs may be most suitable for further experimental validation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a transcriptomic scoring approach to infer glycoRNA-related cellular programs across human tumors, since direct glycoRNA measurement is not feasible in large cancer cohorts. They identified tumor microenvironments enriched for Siglec- and myeloid-associated signatures as the most promising settings for future experimental glycoRNA validation. This is a hypothesis-generating computational study that prioritizes cancer contexts for follow-up glycoRNA work.
